chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Brothers Boston and Hosea in the band; T-Bone's stepfather
summary: Boston played piano on the blues jobs, Smith taught brother Hosea bass, and T-Bone insisted on his stepfather Marco Washington.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, when these acts would come in, like Jimmy Witherspoon or T-Bone, you would be responsible... Would it just be you that would go with them?
No.
Or would you have to actually fix the group?
No. I had the band.
I mean, you wouldn't put Boston in on piano with them.
Boston on piano. Yeah, Boston was on piano with most of them.
Really?
Mmm-hmm.
And could he cope with that?
Yeah. See, they wasn't playin' nothin' but the blues nohow. Most of them was all blues, bluesmen. He controlled them jobs.
And the other brother would be playing bass?

No. T-Bone had a stepdaddy called Marco Washington. He's dead, too. And I used him... I'd use him in the big band, too, before Boston and before my brother started playing. His name was Marco Washington.
And your brother's name? The bass player.
Buster Smith - 201

His name is Hosea Smith. He wasn't playing bass them. So I learned him how to play bass. Just made him go downtown and buy one, and then started him on the bass. Then after Marco got sick... T-Bone wanted to use Marco with him all the time anyhow.
He wanted a good bass player.

No. He couldn't read at all. And he wasn't as good as Hosea. He couldn't read and he didn't have no (?). But he was just a good man, and he was T-Bone's stepdaddy, and we'd go along with it. T-Bone wanted to use him because this was his stepdaddy.
I would have thought T-Bone would have been fussy about his bass players.
No.
He was a good guitar player.
Yeah, he sure was.
A good musician.
Yeah.
He used to be a dancer around here.
